- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for risk premium or reversal.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show upward trend, model often fails to revert; apply downward adjustment of 0.5–2% in 4–6th day.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to over-predict late-period (last 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; reduce final 3–5 days by 0.5–1.5%.
- If sentiment history shows “reversal” (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.7), model often misses the pivot; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to align with sentiment shift.
